summary.text: 左 is based on an early graph interpreted as a left hand and reported for the direction “left.” Later bronze forms add 工 and are also reported for “assist”; the added element’s role and the relation between these uses remain unsettled.

formation.text: The early graph 𠂇 is interpreted as a picture of a left hand. Later bronze forms add 工. One account links 工 with the assisting use; another analyzes 𠂇 as phonetic, but the evidence does not establish that sound role or whether 工 contributes meaning, sound, or both. The later construction is disputed.

components.text: 𠂇 is interpreted as a picture of a left hand in the early graph. Its modern reading matches 左, but this does not establish a historical phonetic role.

sound.text: The supplied local Unihan rows record the same modern Mandarin reading for 𠂇 and 左. This comparison is current evidence only.

components.text: 工 is reported as an addition in later bronze forms and linked in some explanations with the assisting use. Its role in the graph is unresolved.

sound_limitation.text: The supplied local modern Mandarin readings 工 gōng and 左 zuǒ do not establish a historical phonetic role for 工 in 左; the dossier leaves 工’s role unresolved.

sound.text: The supplied local Unihan rows record the modern Mandarin pair 工 gōng and 左 zuǒ. This pair documents current readings, not a historical sound relationship in 左.

history.text: The recorded script forms include oracle-bone, bronze, Chu bamboo and silk, small-seal, and transmitted dictionary forms. Reports describe an early 𠂇 and later bronze forms with 工, but the script labels do not date the earliest individual example.

The transmitted Shuowen explanation analyzes 左 as 𠂇 plus 工 in connection with assistance. Later commentary distinguishes that assisting interpretation from 𠂇 as the directional form. These are historical explanations of the graph, not direct proof of its earliest construction.
Miswritten forms of 左 are reported in inscriptions, but none is identified as an ancestor of the character’s core form.

uncertainties.text: No individually dated oracle-bone example establishes the character’s absolute earliest attestation.

The evidence does not resolve whether 工 contributes meaning, sound, or both in later forms. The proposed phonetic role for 𠂇 lacks an independent historical reading comparison; its modern reading match with 左 does not establish that role.
The chronology and semantic relationship between the reported directional and assisting uses remain unresolved.

senses.period: dating unresolved; reported in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions
senses.text: 左 is reported for the direction “left” in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions. The available reports do not date an individual example closely enough to establish the absolute first use.

senses.period: dating unresolved; reported in bronze inscriptions
senses.text: Bronze inscriptions are reported to use 左 for “assist,” as an early written form of 佐. The evidence does not establish when this use began relative to the directional sense.

limitations.text: The available reports do not establish whether “assist” developed from the directional sense or was a distinct use; they also do not establish the earliest dated use.

overview.text: 左 began as a picture of a left hand and was used for “left.” Later bronze forms add 工 and are also reported for “assist,” though the added part’s role is uncertain.

components.text: 𠂇 depicts a left hand. Its modern reading matches 左, but that alone does not show that it served as a sound cue in the early graph.
工 appears in later bronze forms and is linked with “assist,” though its precise role is unresolved.

relationships.text: In the reported early form of 左, 𠂇 is interpreted as a picture of a left hand.
